subject: the roi math on pro
preheader: 200 a year. one caught mistake pays it forever.
headline: $200/yr to avoid one $20,000 mistake. The math is silly.
body: A bad rental deal costs you, on average, somewhere between $15,000 and $40,000 over the first three years. Negative cash flow, an unexpected CapEx, a refinance that doesn't pencil, a property tax reassessment you didn't model. Pick your poison.
TrueCap Pro is $200/yr. If it catches ONE bad deal — one deal you would've bought without it — it has paid for itself for roughly the next 100 years.

I'm not promising it will catch a bad deal for everyone. Some of you have a great spreadsheet and a sharp brain and you'd catch the mistake anyway. But for most working investors analyzing real deals on real timelines, something falls through the cracks twice a year. PM fees underestimated. Insurance creep. A tax reassessment. DSCR not stress-tested.
$200 vs $20,000+ is not a close decision. It's the cheapest insurance policy in real estate.
Free tier remains free. You don't need to upgrade. But if you've been on the fence, this is the math.
